response:
No, it does not follow that the B_n converge uniformly.

To see why, consider the sequence of polynomials B_n(x) = x^n. This sequence converges pointwise to the function f(x) = 0 on [0, 1]. However, the sequence does not converge uniformly.

To see why, suppose that the sequence B_n converges uniformly to f(x). Then, for any ε > 0, there exists N such that for all n > N, |B_n(x) - f(x)| < ε for all x in [0, 1].

However, for any ε > 0, we can choose x = 1. Then, |B_n(1) - f(1)| = |1^n - 0| = 1, which is not less than ε for any ε > 0. This contradicts the assumption that the sequence B_n converges uniformly to f(x).

Therefore, the sequence B_n does not converge uniformly, even though it converges pointwise to f(x).
